articles.title: Your skin’s chemistry may affect which mosquitoes you attract
articles.snippet: Three species picked their favorite human targets based on skin odor and bacteria. The findings could lead to the design of better repellents.

articles.title: Circular cities go ‘green’ by reusing things over and over again
articles.snippet: To cut their wastes to nearly zero, circular cities are launching projects to repair, reuse and recycle virtually everything.

articles.title: Explainer: What is an equation?
articles.snippet: A mathematical statement, it tells us two expressions are in balance, or equal. So it can help us calculate unknowns from what we already know.

articles.title: Sliding down surfaces can make rainwater corrosive
articles.snippet: Water droplets can take on an electric charge when they slide across objects. Charged rain may start to eat through bridges, cars and more, new data show.

articles.title: Let’s learn about hydrogels
articles.snippet: These polymer-based materials can sop up a lot of water — making them useful for a wide array of tasks.

articles.title: Newfound clouds of missing ‘ordinary’ matter sit outside galaxies
articles.snippet: Dark matter isn’t the universe’s only “missing” matter. Distant bursts of radio waves have now turned up vast, faint gas clouds surrounding galaxies.

articles.title: Scientists Say: Blood Falls
articles.snippet: This five-story-tall waterfall in Antarctica gets its blood-red color from the same reaction that creates rust.

articles.title: In the heat, this Death Valley shrub air conditions its leaves
articles.snippet: Leaves of the Arizona honeysweet can turn on evaporative cooling to keep the plant up to 13 degrees C (23 degrees F) cooler than the surrounding air.

articles.title: Calls of the wild offer sound guidance for protecting animals
articles.snippet: The wild world is full of roars, whoops and songs. Scientists are using such sounds to guide efforts to help save species at threat of extinction.

articles.title: Bees may survive a swim by heading for the dark [COMIC]
articles.snippet: Researchers recently learned that bees can swim. New findings show that bees paddle toward shade and dark to reach shore.

articles.title: Is AI making us dumber? Depends how it’s used
articles.snippet: AI can weaken learning when it replaces effort. But tools that offer guidance rather than answers can help people hone their skills.

articles.title: And the science Nobels for 2026 go to …
articles.snippet: Top prizes went for an icy window into the cosmos, a light switch for the brain and solving the mystery of mirror image molecules.
